text:
Pittsburgh arrives stung by a 4-3 overtime loss to Utah, where Logan Cooley's three goals and Mikhail Sergachev's winner undid a third-period lead. The Penguins are 2-2-1 in their last five and without Bryan Rust, Elmer Soderblom and Trevor van Riemsdyk. Montreal has won four straight, 5-2 at Dallas last time out, even though Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov are hurt. Cole Caufield has stepped into Demidov's spot beside Juraj Slafkovský and Alex Newhook. The teams met on Oct. 3, when Pittsburgh won 6-5 in overtime.

The chance numbers are close: Pittsburgh has taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) at five on five, Montreal 54%. Our model has it 3.21 to 3.19 for the home side. The edge is in net. Projected Canadiens starter Jacob Fowler is at 9.9 goals saved above expected this season, while Arturs Silovs (also projected) is at 2.2 and sat at minus 12.8 last year. Montreal's 5.0 penalties a game remain a worry.

Caufield is our top scorer pick at 38%, and Slafkovský is at 27%. For Pittsburgh, Sidney Crosby is at 30% to score and Rickard Rakell at 31%, with Tommy Novak, who has absorbed Rust's minutes, one assist from 100. Among our under-the-radar picks, Montreal's Alexandre Texier has dangerous shots for a third-liner (14% to score), and Ben Kindel is at 48% for a point after moving into Pittsburgh's top six.
